stemBlocks.value: A tourist exchanges US$1 200 at US$1 = J$155 and a tax of 2% is charged. (a) Calculate the amount in Jamaican dollars before tax. (b) Calculate the tax. (c) Calculate the final amount received.
Think first: Convert first, then tax: the 2% is charged on the Jamaican dollar amount the conversion produced.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p021-q24 from workbook page 21.

solutionSteps.instruction: Convert US dollars to Jamaican dollars.
Subtract the tax from the amount before tax.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply US$1 200 by 155 to convert, take 2% of that result as tax, then subtract the tax from the converted amount.

whyThisWorks.value: The tax is a charge on the transaction, so it is calculated on the full converted value and then removed from what the tourist walks away with. Because 2% is deducted, 98% remains, which is why the single multiplier 0.98 reproduces the final figure. Taxing the US dollar amount would give an answer in the wrong currency.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking 2% of US$1 200 and mixing currencies.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking 2% of US$1 200 and mixing currencies.
